ai.title: Add x-session-affinity header to Fireworks requests
ai.summary: Fireworks API requests now include an x-session-affinity header set to the user ID. This change propagates the sessionId through createFireworksRequest and createFireworksRequestWithFallback in web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts. The header enables better prompt caching on the Fireworks backend by associating requests with specific sessions.

eli5.text: Each time you send a message and the assistant replies, the request now includes your unique user ID as a label. This lets the system group your requests together so it can remember and reuse parts of previous conversations more efficiently. If you use Fireworks-powered features, you may notice responses feel slightly faster or more consistent because the system recognizes your session. This is active for all users today.

ai.title: Fix build in fireworks-deployment tests
ai.summary: Added missing sessionId parameter to test calls in web/src/llm-api/__tests__/fireworks-deployment.test.ts. This fixes build errors caused by type mismatches in test mocks. Scope limited to test files.

eli5.text: The automated test scripts that check the Fireworks connection were updated to pass along a session identifier field they were missing. This fixes a build error that was caused by type mismatches in the test mocks. If you look at the project's build logs, the Fireworks tests now compile and run successfully where they previously failed.

ai.title: Add session affinity and usage stats metrics to scripts
ai.summary: Scripts query-usage-stats.ts and test-fireworks-long.ts updated. query-usage-stats.ts adds median and max requests per client to SQL and output. test-fireworks-long.ts adds x-session-affinity header for prompt caching.

eli5.text: When you run a long test chat against our internal benchmarking tool, each consecutive message now carries a shared session tag in its header so the service consistently routes all turns to the same backend machine. That machine already cached earlier prompts in the conversation, so follow-up questions reuse that cache instead of recomputing them from scratch, which is what makes longer test conversations faster and cheaper to evaluate. Separately, our internal usage stats dashboard now reports the median and peak number of requests per active client, not just the average, giving a clearer picture when a few heavy clients skew the numbers. Both changes affect only the tooling and dashboards used by our own engineers; no customer-facing behavior was altered.

ai.title: Move analytics init to initializeApp
ai.summary: Refactored CLI startup to move `initAnalytics` from `main` in `cli/src/index.tsx` to `initializeApp` in `cli/src/init/init-app.ts`. This ensures analytics are initialized before `initializeDirenv`, preventing errors when the logger calls `trackEvent` during direnv setup. The `APP_LAUNCHED` event tracking in `index.tsx` now relies on the initialization state established by `initializeApp`.

eli5.text: When the app starts up, it now sets up its tracking/analytics features earlier in the startup sequence, right before it prepares the development environment tools. This prevents startup errors that happened when the environment setup tried to log activity before tracking was ready. Users on CLI v1.0.632 may notice fewer startup warnings when direnv initialization runs alongside other startup checks.

ai.title: Add header-based country detection fallback for free mode
ai.summary: Chat completions API now prioritizes `cf-ipcountry` and `x-vercel-ip-country` headers over GeoIP lookup for free mode gating. The `getCountryCode` helper replaces `getCountryFromIp`, filtering out 'XX' and 'T1' placeholders before falling back to IP resolution. Updates `web/src/app/api/v1/chat/completions/_post.ts` with structured logging for header and GeoIP results to aid debugging.

eli5.text: When you send a free-mode request to the chat API, the server now first checks two special headers from the network edge ({ "headers": {"cf-ipcountry": "Cloudflare", "x-vercel-ip-country": "Vercel"} }) that tell it your country before falling back to a slower IP-based lookup. If either header reports a real country code (anything other than the placeholder {"values": ["XX", "T1"]}), that code is used; otherwise it keeps using the old IP method. You would not see any visible change in your chat experience. The server is now also logging which country-detection method it tried, so developers can debug why a request was or was not allowed through free-mode gating. This is live today for free-mode users who hit the chat completions endpoint.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.632 Release Bump
ai.summary: Released Freebuff 1.0.632, bundling the previous day's user-visible work across CLI, agents, web, and CI packages. Notable additions include Browser Use subagent with Chrome detection gating, /connect slash command, paste-to-attach file handling, header-based country detection fallback for free mode, and e2e tests now required before releases. Internal tooling gained usage stats scripts, CanopyWave caching benchmark, and checkoutref support in the release workflow.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json: version field changed from "1.0.631" to "1.0.632" (+1/-1)

eli5.text: This release adds browser automation so you can have an AI agent open websites and interact with web pages using Chrome, plus a new 'librarian' helper that can clone and read through GitHub code repositories to answer questions about them. You can now paste file paths directly into the chat to attach documents or code files for discussion, and the command list has been reorganized so the interview workflow is easier to find. Behind the scenes, the release process now requires passing end-to-end tests before deploying, which helps make sure each version is more stable and secure. The terminal interface also shows better visual feedback when agents are working, with a subtle shimmer animation that tells you processing is happening in real time.

ai.title: Add /connect to Freebuff-only command sets
ai.summary: Added 'connect' to FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMANDS in cli/src/commands/command-registry.ts and FREEBUFF_ONLY_COMMAND_IDS in cli/src/data/slash-commands.ts. Ensures /connect is treated as a Freebuff-exclusive command alongside /plan. Scope limited to CLI command registry and slash command data definitions.

eli5.text: The 'connect' command now works exclusively for one specific type of customer, the same group that already had access to the 'plan' command. If you tried to use 'connect' outside that group, it would stop working. The change is live today and affects only that group's access.

ai.title: Add MiniMax cache stats script and fix usage stats denominator
ai.summary: Added scripts/query-minimax-cache-stats.ts to report overall and per-client cache hit rates for minimax/minimax-m2.5 over the last 19 hours. Updated scripts/query-usage-stats.ts to calculate average input tokens and cache rates using only `input_tokens` as the denominator, excluding `cache_read_input_tokens` and `cache_creation_input_tokens` from the total. This aligns usage metrics with standard cache efficiency calculations.

eli5.text: You can now check how often responses to you from the minimax and minimax-m2.5 models are being pulled from a fast cache instead of being generated fresh, with reports broken out by each individual customer using the service. At the same time, the numbers that measure how efficiently these cached responses are being used were quietly being calculated incorrectly, the math was accidentally counting the cached text twice, which made the system look either more or less efficient than it really was. The fix adjusts those figures so they reflect only the new text actually typed out, giving a truer picture of how much time and computing power the caching is really saving. ai.title: Revamped context pruner: separate budgets and back-walk
ai.summary: Context pruner overhauled to use separate token budgets for user messages (50k) and assistant/tool content (20k), replacing previous character limits. The new algorithm builds summaries by walking backward from the most recent message to preserve recency. This change affects agents/context-pruner.ts, introducing constants like USER_BUDGET and TOOL_ENTRY_LIMIT while removing helper functions like truncateLongText from the main scope.

eli5.text: When an AI runs a long conversation that would otherwise exceed its memory limits, it now keeps more of your recent messages intact instead of chopping them off. The system first sets aside room for your side of the conversation (up to 50,000 tokens) and a smaller pool for its own replies and tool usage (up to 20,000 tokens), then trims older content by summarizing from the latest message backward so the most recent exchange stays complete. You would notice fewer cases where a response suddenly drops out mid-conversation or loses the immediate context it was responding to.

ai.title: context-pruner: Include edit results, exclude librarian, tmux-cli
ai.summary: context-pruner now serializes full JSON results for str_replace, propose_str_replace, write_file, and propose_write_file into the summary, replacing the previous diff-only extraction. This ensures edit outcomes are preserved when pruning context. The pruner also excludes librarian, tmux-cli, and browser-use from its processing scope.
